blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The fork: BSc jobs and MSc-only doors

rows: IIT JAM, Chemistry paper

Apply through JAM 2027 (IIT Kharagpur). Applications close on 19 October 2026, the exam is on 14 February 2027 and results come on 18 March 2027. About 3,000 seats across participating IITs. Each admitting institute sets its own subject rule, so read the eligibility page for your target programme.
A final-year or finished BSc can apply. Qualifying is not admission.
GATE 2027

The official eligibility table lets students of a three-year BSc sit GATE in the third year or after finishing, to seek master's admission at IITs and IISc. There is a Chemistry (CY) paper, and the Life Sciences (XL) paper carries a 25-mark Chemistry section.
You can appear. It does not open jobs that name an MSc, such as BARC or DRDO.
CSIR-UGC NET (JRF and PhD)
A master's at 55 percent (50 percent for reserved categories), or a four-year bachelor's at 75 percent. JRF age limit is 30, with up to 5 years of relaxation for listed categories.
A plain three-year BSc does not qualify.
BARC OCES-2026, Chemistry

MSc or integrated MSc in Chemistry with 60 percent in the MSc and 60 percent in the BSc, Physics up to BSc level and Mathematics at Class 12 or BSc level. Age up to 26 for the general category on 1 August 2026.
Not eligible without the MSc.
DRDO Scientist B
Reported as a first-class master's in Chemistry plus a valid GATE Chemistry score. The detailed advertisement appears on rac.gov.in when DRDO posts it, so read that notice.
Not eligible without the MSc.
Food Analyst under FSSAI rules

A master's in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Microbiology, Dairy Chemistry or Food Technology (and a few equivalents), at least three years of experience in analysing food, and a pass in the board that FSSAI notifies.
Not eligible. A BSc can start the three-year clock only after the master's.

FSSAI Food Analyst, short-term contract
₹60,000 x 12 = ₹7,20,000 a year, about 2.5 times the Payscale average. It needs a master's, three years of food analysis and a board pass.

₹74,000 x 12 = ₹8,88,000 a year, about 3.1 times the Payscale average. It comes with a three-year bond and an MSc with 60 percent.

Read ten live postings for each.
Make one piece of proof for each.
